meta.purpose: Single onboarding file. Any agent should be able to read this + the other state files and fully understand the project's evolution, current state, and why things are the way they are.

summary.what: One-paragraph plain-language description of the project as it stands today.

timeline.title: EXAMPLE: Project initialized from AI Guidance baseline.
timeline.detail: What happened and why it matters for future agents.

timeline.title: Enforcement layer + auto KPI-snapshot added.
timeline.detail: Git hooks (pre-commit validate, pre-push gate on v* tags), CI (state-validation, lighthouse-ci, kpi-snapshot), and scripts (validate_state, check_release_gate, snapshot_kpis) make state integrity and release gates machine-enforced. KPI snapshots, memory entries, and status resets now run automatically on release tags. Resolved debt-001.

timeline.title: Reference metric fetcher wired into the snapshot pipeline.
timeline.detail: scripts/fetch_metrics.py (+ fetch_metrics.sh wrapper) reads kpis.json and queries each KPI's instrumentation.source — Amplitude (event segmentation), Supabase (PostgREST count), CrUX (field p75). Wired into kpi-snapshot.yml before the snapshot step. Unconfigured/erroring sources are omitted and carried forward, so the release pipeline is now fully turnkey without ever blocking on metric retrieval. Seed kpis.json now uses concrete sources + fetch config.

timeline.title: Architecture description made a hard release gate
timeline.detail: Added docs/architecture/overview.md as a required, gate-enforced file. check_release_gate.py now blocks releases unless the architecture doc exists, has no placeholders, and has real substance (file-based, can't be faked). Wired into CLAUDE.md Pre-Flight + release gates, rules/01, and the architecture README. See dec-003.

timeline.title: Project identity authored in Markdown (PROJECT.md -> project.json)
timeline.detail: Added PROJECT.md as the human authoring surface and scripts/sync_project.py to compile it into .ai/state/project.json (still the machine source of truth). bootstrap.sh init copies PROJECT.md + runs sync; added `bootstrap.sh sync`; pre-commit regenerates + re-stages project.json so the two never drift. project.json is now generated — never hand-edited. See dec-004.

timeline.title: Export contract added (praxis-export.json) for dashboards
timeline.detail: scripts/export_state.py emits a stable, versioned projection of all state: export_contract_version, uid='<slug>:<id>' namespacing, precomputed summary rollups, and a flattened links[] relationship graph. Schema at .ai/schemas/praxis-export.schema.json; `bootstrap.sh export`; gitignored by default. Foundation for a separate admin dashboard (static read / Supabase projection). See dec-005.

timeline.title: Fix: State Validation CI failed on the baseline itself
timeline.detail: state-validation.yml ran validate_state.py --strict, which fails on REPLACE_* placeholders. The Praxis baseline is a TEMPLATE that intentionally keeps placeholders, so CI failed on every push. Fix: validate_state.py now honors the .praxis-template marker — when present, --strict placeholder failures downgrade to warnings (JSON/schema/dup-ID checks still apply). Real projects (no marker) stay strictly enforced. Same lesson as the release-gate exemption: the tool that enforces discipline must know when it is operating on the template vs a product.

learnings.lesson: EXAMPLE: a non-obvious thing learned that should not be re-learned the hard way.

Any check that enforces 'real project' discipline (strict placeholder validation, release gates) must distinguish template vs product via the .praxis-template marker, or it will fail on the baseline repo itself.
learnings.context: State Validation CI failed on every Praxis push because --strict rejects the template's intentional REPLACE_* placeholders.
